newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian farmers' unions call for milk fines delay.
newsitem.headline: Italian farmers' unions call for milk fines delay.

text.p: Italian farmers' unions called on Tuesday for the deadline for paying first instalments of European Union fines for overshooting strict milk output quotas to be put back.
"The presidents asked the government to push back the deadline of payments for the fine set for May 10," the union leaders said after a meeting.

The call came as a special Italian government commission released its findings on the milk disputes, which erupted after farmers refused to pay the 192.2 million Ecus ($167 million) EU fines earlier this year.
Farmers blockaded roads and airports in northern Italy in January to protest against the fine and accused the government of failing to advise them of their correct quotas.
The commission told parliament on Tuesday that the government and producers were to blame for missing milk quotas in 1995/96.
"The state did not have an effective output control mechanism...and (the unions) failed to give an overview of the situation," the report said.

Italy passed a package of emergency aid measures for the dairy sector following the farmers' protests. They included provisions for cheap loans, payments of fines by instalment and a pledge to set up a commission to examine grievances.
The commission said Italy had asked the European Commission to increase its milk quotas as the country "certainly did not produce enough milk for itself".
